notes: [OTDV]: the DV document 'expands the testplan inline, in addition to capturing the overall strategy ... It also covers FPV goals, if applicable' (the DV document section). The page also names Formal Property Verification as one of two key techniques, with JasperGold and VC Formal as FPV tools; the document's sentence says nothing beyond the DV-document point, so it is supported as worded. The testplan is described as tests plus functional coverage; the page does not put FPV in the testplan, and the document no longer says it does.

[SbyRef]: the mode option is mandatory with values bmc, prove, live, cover, prep, as the document says for the three it names; depth: 'bmc, cover: Only the specified number of cycles are considered. Default: 20' and 'prove: Depth for the k-induction performed by the smtbmc engine. Other engines ignore this option in prove mode. Default: 20' match the document's depth sentence. The document does not name live or prep; the gate's 'another mode' branch covers them.

[SbyQuick]: 'Reached cover statement at w_underfill in step 2' with a trace written to a VCD file, and the first-cycle $past reading X (so a past_nwen register is used), support the cover-trace and $past-guard sentences. The page says the default tasks are basic and cover and that bmc and cover run to depth 20 by default, as the reference does.

[ZFormal]: a bounded check can miss states reached later than its depth; induction can start from an unreachable state unless unreachable states are declared invalid; assume() is forced true and not proven; $past is undefined before the first clock and the author uses an f_past_valid register; the FIFO example asserts helper relations (f_fill == r_fill and the pointer relations) beside the interface properties. All on the page. The sentence 'bounds on counters' is the document's reading of those helper asserts; fair, inference-level.

A check beyond the claims: real runs of the formal gate pass on this machine (tests/test_nirmaan_gate_integrity.py::test_bmc_is_reported_as_bounded_and_does_not_meet_the_formal_gate runs sby in bmc and prove mode on the same false assertion: bmc passes with 'no counterexample within 3 steps' and proven 0, prove fails). tests/test_nirmaan_gates_rest.py cover and antecedent tests (14 selected) run real sby cover and pass.

Imprecision, not a failure: 'a setup with no cover at all fails too' is true of the setup's own covers: parse_sby_cover tests `if not reached`, and `reached` holds only the seat's own covers, not the derived antecedent covers (eda_parsers.py:432-434). A setup with assertions but no own cover therefore fails even when every derived antecedent cover is reached. The sentence does not say otherwise.
